nodes.title:
Remote Code Execution (RCE) Vulnerability Summary:
       - Vulnerability: Misconfigurations in the Java Management Extensions (JMX) framework can lead to Remote Code Execution (RCE) in a Java RMI (Remote Method Invocation) service.
       - Impact: An unauthenticated remote attacker can gain administrative privileges and execute arbitrary code on the compromised system.
       - JMX: Provides a standard way to monitor and manage Java applications, devices, and service-oriented networks.
       - RMI: Allows an object running in one Java Virtual Machine (JVM) to invoke methods on an object running in another JVM.
       - Core Vulnerability: Insecure configurations, most commonly the lack of authentication and/or improper network exposure. 
       - Exploitation: An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by interacting with the `MBeanServer` through the exposed RMI interface.
       - Malicious MBeans for RCE: The `MLet` MBean is designed to load other MBeans from a remote URL. An attacker can use this to execute arbitrary code on the victim server.
       - Problem: Many applications and systems have been found vulnerable due to these insecure JMX/RMI configurations.
       - Mitigation and Prevention: Enable Authentication, Implement Authorization/Access Control, Network Segmentation and Firewalls, Use Secure Transport (SSL/TLS), Principle of Least Privilege, Regular Updates and Patching, Disable Unnecessary Functionality, Avoid Remote MLet Loading, and Security Audits.
